sources.entry: Maddy Mail Server - All-in-one mail server that implements SMTP (both MTA and MX) and IMAP. Replaces Postfix, Dovecot, OpenDKIM, OpenSPF, OpenDMARC with single daemon. (Source Code) GPL-3.0 Go

summary.one_liner: Maddy is a composable all-in-one mail server that handles SMTP (MTA and MX), IMAP storage, and email authentication standards in a single Go daemon.
summary.what_it_does: Maddy sends messages over SMTP (acting as an MTA) and accepts incoming messages over SMTP (acting as an MX). It stores messages and provides access to them via IMAP. The README says it also implements DKIM, SPF, DMARC, DANE, and MTA-STS to support email security. It is positioned as a replacement for Postfix, Dovecot, OpenDKIM, OpenSPF, and OpenDMARC, using one daemon with uniform configuration. The README gives no detail on specific configuration options beyond linking to a setup tutorial and documentation.
use_cases: replace Postfix and Dovecot with one daemon
send and receive email for my domain
serve IMAP mailboxes to email clients
set up DKIM, SPF and DMARC signing and checking
self-hosted mail for a small organization
how_to_run: Follow the setup tutorial linked from the README
Consult the documentation linked from the README
notable: Single daemon replaces several separate mail components (Postfix, Dovecot, OpenDKIM, OpenSPF, OpenDMARC)
Covers both sending (MTA) and receiving (MX) over SMTP
Implements DKIM, SPF, DMARC, DANE and MTA-STS
caveats: IMAP storage is described as beta in the README
README recommends Dovecot if a stable, feature-packed IMAP server is needed
Running a mail server requires separate setup per the linked tutorial (details not in README)
